Finding Hope Together Through Faith-Based Support

Christian counselling services can give couples a space to slow down, talk honestly and invite God into the middle of their struggles. When work, school and family demands keep piling up, it is common to feel distant from the person you love most. Arguments seem to repeat, small issues grow bigger and prayer as a couple may feel awkward or missing. In these moments, many couples start to wonder if there is a safe place to talk about both their relationship and their faith at the same time.

That is where Christian couples counselling can help. It brings your beliefs, values and emotions into one honest conversation. In this article, we will look at what Christian counselling services for couples are like, what makes them different, common struggles they can address and how to tell if it might be the right fit for your relationship in Brisbane and beyond.

What Makes Christian Couples Counselling Different

Christian couples counselling sits at the meeting point of psychological science and faith. It does not replace your walk with God or your church life, but it adds structured support with a trained professional.

In Christian counselling services for couples, we usually focus on three key areas at once:

  • Emotional support and understanding
  • Practical tools for communication and problem-solving
  • Reflection on God’s design for loving, faithful relationships

Prayer, Scripture and spiritual practices can be part of the process, if you want them to be. Some couples like to open or close sessions with prayer. Others prefer to talk about how their faith shapes decisions without praying out loud. Both are welcome.

A few important points about faith in sessions:

  • Your beliefs are respected, not forced or judged
  • We work with your own level of faith and church involvement
  • Couples from different Christian traditions are welcome
  • If one partner is not Christian, the focus is on shared values, care and respect

The aim is not to “win” a theological debate, but to help both partners grow in love, understanding and unity in a way that honours God and honours each other.

Common Relationship Struggles Faith-Filled Couples Face

Being Christian does not remove stress, hurt or conflict from a relationship. In fact, sometimes faith adds extra pressure, as couples feel they “should” be doing better.

Christian couples often come to counselling for issues such as:

  • Ongoing arguments that never seem to resolve
  • Communication that feels sharp, defensive or shut down
  • Emotional disconnection and feeling more like housemates
  • Parenting stress and different approaches to discipline
  • Financial worries that trigger blame or anxiety
  • Intimacy concerns, both physical and emotional

There can also be faith-related tensions, for example:

  • One partner wants to be more involved at church, the other is tired or unsure
  • Different views on how decisions should be made in the home
  • Confusion around roles, leadership and service in the relationship
  • Guilt or shame around sex, forgiveness or past choices

Life transitions can stir things up as well. Changes in work hours, children starting or changing schools, or a shift in health can all make old cracks in the relationship feel wider. When energy is low, and stress is high, it is easy to drift into resentment, silence or quick tempers.

Christian counselling services can give you space to talk about big questions too. Many couples wrestle with disappointment, grief or prayers that feel unanswered. Gentle support can help you make sense of suffering together, rather than turning against each other or pulling away from God.

Inside a Christian Counselling Session for Couples

The first appointment is usually about feeling safe and heard. Your psychologist will offer a warm welcome and explain how sessions work. You will both have time to share what has been happening and what you are hoping for. Together, you and your psychologist can agree on how openly you want to include prayer, Scripture or Christian resources.

Early sessions often include:

  • Listening carefully to both partners’ stories
  • Clarifying shared goals and areas of tension
  • Setting some basic ground rules so conversations feel respectful and safe

As sessions continue, you may:

  • Learn new ways to speak so your partner can really hear you
  • Practise listening without interrupting or defending
  • Work on calming conflict before it gets too heated
  • Set faith-aligned boundaries around time, technology, money or family
  • Create small, daily habits that build connection and trust

The psychologist’s role is to stay neutral, compassionate and steady. They are there for both of you, not to “take sides” or decide who is right. They help you slow down, notice unhelpful patterns and try different ways of relating.

Some couples choose to include specific Christian practices, such as:

  • Praying together in session, especially during hard conversations
  • Reflecting on Bible passages about love, grace and humility
  • Structured forgiveness work when there has been hurt or betrayal
  • Gratitude exercises that focus on God’s goodness and your partner’s strengths

All of these are optional. You stay in control of what feels respectful and helpful for your faith.

How Michelle Barratt Psychology Supports Brisbane Couples

At Michelle Barratt Psychology, we offer Christian counselling services as part of our broader clinical psychology practice for children, adolescents, adults, couples and families. Our team provides support from clinics in Toowong and Wynnum West, as well as through Telehealth for couples across Brisbane and regional Queensland.

Our work with couples is grounded in:

  • Evidence-based approaches from relationship and mental health research
  • Trauma-informed care that takes past hurts seriously
  • An understanding of how faith can shape both pain and hope

Many couples coming to counselling are also parents. We pay close attention to how your relationship patterns affect the whole family system. Sessions can include age-appropriate ways to think about parenting, boundaries and emotional safety for children.

Seeing a clinical psychologist who understands both psychological science and Christian belief can be especially helpful when there are deeper issues in the background, such as:

  • Anxiety or depression in one or both partners
  • Previous trauma, including childhood or relationship trauma
  • Grief, loss or big life changes affecting your connection

Appointments can be arranged to fit around work hours, school runs and family routines, with the option to meet in person or online if travel or childcare is difficult.

Signs It May Be Time to Seek Christian Couples’ Support

Many couples wait until a crisis before asking for help. Often, the earlier you come, the easier it is to shift patterns.

Some clear signs you might benefit from Christian couples counselling are:

  • Frequent arguments that end with no real resolution
  • Feeling like you are walking on eggshells at home
  • Living more like housemates, with little affection or fun
  • Struggling to pray together or talk about faith without tension

There are also quieter warning signs, such as:

  • Growing resentment that never gets named or healed
  • One or both partners withdrawing and keeping everything inside
  • Using work, social media, ministry or hobbies to avoid being home
  • Secret habits that you know are pulling you away from your partner

Seeking help is not a sign of spiritual failure. It is a step of courage and good stewardship of a relationship that is precious to you and to God. Choosing to get support before things feel unbearable can protect your connection and give you room to grow, rather than only trying to “fix” things in a crisis.

Taking the Next Step Toward Healing and Connection

If your relationship has felt strained, it can be helpful to pause and ask God to show you what is really going on in your heart and in your home. You might want to take a quiet moment to reflect on questions like: Where are we struggling? Where are we strong? What do we hope our relationship will look like in the months ahead?

A simple next step can be to talk honestly with your partner about the idea of Christian couples counselling and what you both would hope to gain from it. At Michelle Barratt Psychology, we offer Christian counselling services for couples from our Toowong and Wynnum West locations, as well as through Telehealth for those who prefer online support or live farther away. Whether you feel ready to start soon or are only just beginning to think about it, know that help is available and change is possible, one small, faithful step at a time.

Take The Next Step Toward Faith-Centred Support

If you feel it is time to explore therapy that respects and integrates your Christian faith, we are here to walk alongside you. At Michelle Barratt Psychology, our Christian counselling services are designed to support your emotional, psychological and spiritual wellbeing. You are welcome to reach out to discuss your situation or arrange an appointment, and we will respond with options that suit your needs and schedule. If you are ready to connect, please contact us to get started.
